const path = require('path')
console.log(path.posix.relative('/a/b', '/a/b/c'))

const path = require('path')
console.log(path.posix.normalize('/a/../b'))
console.log(Buffer.compare(Buffer.from('a'), Buffer.from('a')))
console.log(Buffer.from('ab').equals(Buffer.from('ab')) ? 1 : 0)

setImmediate(() => console.log(1))
setImmediate(() => console.log(2))

setImmediate(() => console.log(1))
Promise.resolve().then(() => console.log(2))

const buf = Buffer.alloc(2)
buf.writeUInt8(7, 1)
console.log(buf[0])
console.log(buf[1])
console.log(Buffer.from('abcd').indexOf(Buffer.from('cd')))

const buf = Buffer.alloc(2)
buf.fill(3)
console.log(buf[0])
console.log(buf[1])

const crypto = require('crypto')
console.log(crypto.createHash('sha256').update('a').digest('hex').slice(0, 2))
console.log(Buffer.byteLength('0a', 'hex'))

const path = require('path')
console.log(path.posix.format({ dir: '/a', base: 'b.txt' }))

const u = new URL('https://a.test/x?n=4')
console.log(u.searchParams.get('n'))

const buf = Buffer.from('hi')
console.log(buf.toString('utf8', 1))

Promise.resolve().then(() => console.log(1))
setImmediate(() => console.log(2))

const { Buffer: B } = require('buffer')
console.log(B.from([1, 2]).readUInt8(1))
In which libuv loop phase does setImmediate run?
options: In the check phase, after poll
In the timers phase, before poll

questions.text: What does UV_THREADPOOL_SIZE set?
options: The libuv thread-pool size for some I/O and crypto, not for all JS

questions.text: How does stream.pipeline differ from pipe()?
options: pipe destroys every socket in the process
pipeline forwards errors, destroys streams, and gives a callback/promise when it finishes. pipe does not collect errors for you
There is no difference; they are aliases

questions.text: What is backpressure on a Readable?
options: It is a synonym of HTTP pause()
The consumer cannot keep up. push() returns false when the buffer is above highWaterMark, and reading should slow down

questions.text: How does Buffer.alloc differ from Buffer.allocUnsafe?
options: alloc zero-fills. allocUnsafe is faster but may leave old heap bytes
allocUnsafe is always zeros; alloc is random bytes
alloc cannot be called with a length above 8
They are the same since Node 18

questions.text: What does EventEmitter do when there are too many listeners?
options: After defaultMaxListeners it prints a possible leak warning. emit still runs
The process always exits with code 1

questions.text: How do you get a synchronous require from an ESM file?
options: ESM still has a global require
module.createRequire(import.meta.url) returns a require bound to that file

questions.text: How does child_process.fork differ from spawn?
options: spawn always starts a V8 isolate in the same process
fork is spawn of a node process with an IPC channel. spawn runs any program and has no IPC channel by default

questions.text: How do worker_threads differ from cluster?
options: Workers are threads of one process with a separate V8. cluster is separate processes; memory is not shared
cluster is threads; worker_threads are processes
Both share one heap with no limits
worker_threads cannot be used for CPU work

questions.text: What happens if a rejected promise has no handler?
options: Node emits unhandledRejection on process. That is not the same as a throw in synchronous code

questions.text: What is the exports field in package.json for?
options: It is the list of npm scripts
It sets the package’s public entry points and can block deep paths that used to be reached through main
It is only for a browser bundler; Node ignores it

questions.text: What does the --inspect flag do?
options: It turns on JS strict mode
It compiles the project into one binary
It starts the DevTools protocol so a debugger can attach to the process

questions.text: Does NODE_ENV affect Node core?
options: No. It is a convention of libraries and bundlers. Node core does not switch on it
Yes. production turns off the event loop

questions.text: What does objectMode do on a stream?
options: It serializes objects to JSON on disk
It lets chunks be any JS values, not only Buffer/string
It is a mode only for fs.createWriteStream

questions.text: How does exec differ from spawn?
options: exec only works in the browser
spawn buffers all output into a string; exec streams
exec runs the command through a shell and buffers stdout/stderr. spawn gives streams and does not need a shell
Both always use a shell and the same buffer

questions.text: How do you load an ESM module from CommonJS?
options: Through dynamic import(), which returns a promise. Synchronous require will not load ESM

questions.text: Endless process.nextTick calls can starve libuv phases, including setImmediate.
CPU-heavy code on the JS thread is itself offloaded to the UV threadpool.
fs.promises.readFile does not block the loop during the file read, unlike readFileSync.
AbortController in Node cannot be passed to fetch or to any fs operations.
pipe() does not by itself destroy every stream in the chain when one of them errors.
module.domain is the current way to catch errors in Node 20+.
dns.lookup often uses the threadpool and can clog it under many lookups.
uncaughtException is the normal way to keep an HTTP server running after any throw.
highWaterMark limits a stream’s internal buffer, not the file size on disk.
workerData is cloned into the worker at start; it is not shared memory with the parent by default.
The main field always wins over exports when both are set.
setImmediate from an I/O callback runs in that iteration’s check phase, before the next timers phase.
child_process.exec does not buffer output, so it is safe for gigabyte logs.
A parentPort.postMessage payload is structured-cloned unless you pass a transfer list.
require caches the ESM graph the same way as import, with no exceptions.
fs.createReadStream reads the file in chunks and can respect consumer backpressure.
What are the main libuv loop phases around I/O, in order?
questions.answer: timers, then pending callbacks, poll, check (setImmediate), close.

questions.text: What happens if you queue nextTick forever?
questions.answer: libuv phases and I/O never get a turn. The loop starves.

questions.text: Why use stream.pipeline instead of .pipe() in production?
questions.answer: Errors are forwarded, streams are destroyed, and you get a callback or promise at the end.

questions.text: Why is spawn safer than exec for arguments?
questions.answer: spawn without a shell does not join the command into one string, so injection risk is lower.

questions.text: Do cluster processes share one V8 heap?
questions.answer: No. Each process has its own heap. IPC is messages, not shared memory.

questions.text: What is emitted on process for a throw outside try/catch?
questions.answer: uncaughtException. The process is not considered healthy after that.

questions.text: How do you call ESM from CJS?
questions.answer: Dynamic import(). require will not load an ESM file.

questions.text: What does createRequire(import.meta.url) do?
questions.answer: It gives a require function resolved relative to that ESM file.

questions.text: What is AbortSignal for in Node async APIs?
questions.answer: To cancel work: fetch, some fs APIs, and timers.

questions.text: What is the dual package hazard?
questions.answer: The same package loads as both CJS and ESM — two copies of its state.

questions.text: Why use objectMode on a Transform?
questions.answer: So chunks can be objects, not only bytes and strings.

questions.text: What is EventEmitter’s maxListeners warning about?
questions.answer: A suspected leak: listeners pile up and are never removed.

questions.text: Where does Node run crypto.pbkdf2 by default — JS thread or pool?
questions.answer: On the libuv threadpool, so heavy crypto competes with fs for the pool.

questions.text: Does child_process.spawn use a shell by default?
questions.answer: No. You turn on shell: true explicitly.

questions.text: What does NODE_DEBUG do?
questions.answer: It enables debug logs for built-in modules by name, for example fs, net.

questions.text: How do pause()/resume() on a Readable relate to flowing mode?
questions.answer: resume and a data listener turn on flowing mode. pause stops automatic chunk delivery.
